en: Resplendent with the luster of a young crane, his matted locks are as dark as sapphires; his body is smeared with ashes, and he wears a garment of tiger skin.
His mind and breath are dissolved in peaceful sound, and he puts to shame Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Sanaka, and the other sages; he is worshipped by the Siddhas.
One should always meditate upon Dattātreya for the attainment of one's desired goals— the son of Atri,
who is clothed in space, whose limbs are smeared with ashes, who holds a discus, a trident, a hand-drum, and a mace,
who sits in the lotus posture, and whose eyes are like the moon and the sun.
Oṃ, salutations! I bow to the one bestowed by the venerable Guru; I praise Datta, the God, the Teacher of the World, who is partless and devoid of qualities. I bow to Dattātreya.
I bow to Dattātreya, the Lord of Brahmā, the Lord of the world of light, and the Lord of beings, who bears the conch, the discus, and the mace, and who holds an alms-bowl in his hand.
I bow to Dattātreya, the God worshipped by the Lord of the gods, who is adored by the worlds of the three realms, and whose very essence is both Hari and Hara.
Stainless and blue-hued, beautiful and graced with a dark complexion, with lovely eyes and wide-open gaze—I bow to Dattātreya.
Adorned with a trident, a hand-drum, and a garland, and crowned with matted locks; adorned with earrings upon his ears—I bow to Dattātreya.
His body embellished with sacred ashes, beautified by necklaces and armlets, having the form of the infinite Praṇava—I bow to Śrī Dattātreya.
I bow to Dattātreya, the god of serene countenance, the bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation, the one who increases the prosperity of people, the protector of the world.

I bow to Dattātreya, the king of kings, whose conduct is primordial, the granter of boons to Kārtavīrya, the most auspicious and benevolent Subhadra. I bow to Dattātreya, the beloved of Anasūyā, the son of Atri, the lord of gods, the renowned liberation of the yogis. I bow to Dattātreya.

I bow to Dattātreya, the best of embodied beings, who is clothed in the directions (naked), established in the state of Brahman, eternal, and possessed of the *haṃsa* (the supreme self) and the conch (purity). Sometimes a yogi, sometimes a seeker of enjoyment, delighting in the playful sports of a child, with teeth resembling jewels—I bow to Dattātreya. O dispeller of the fear of existence caused by spirits and winds, likewise [protector] from the affliction of planetary influences; O destroyer of poverty and pride—I bow to Dattātreya.
On the fourteenth day, on a Wednesday, in the auspicious month of Mārgaśīrṣa, my birth occurred. I bow to the vast Sāraka; I salute Dattātreya.
His feet are like the petals of a red lotus, the source of all sacred pilgrimage sites (tīrthas). Saluted by yogis and the wise, I salute Dattātreya.
He is the manifest Lord, the giver of knowledge, the refuge, and the bestower of liberation. Self-born, the Lord, Kṛṣṇaka—Dattātreya, I salute him.

This is the *Bhṛgūvinicita*, this is the *Dattātreya-pārāyaṇa*. Dattātreya is Brahmā himself; I bow to Dattātreya. By the hymn of praise (*stuti-stotra*) to Dattātreya, which shatters the bonds of karma for all living beings and creatures, one attains all desires and merit.
One obtains a son who is wise and virtuous, endowed with wealth and grain; one becomes a king, and Lakṣmī [fortune] attends him. A human being attains even that which was previously unattainable.

One who constantly recites this hymn of praise to Dattātreya three times a day shall have no fear of disease; he shall become long-lived and victorious. Kuṣmāṇḍas, Ḍākinīs, Bhakṣakas, Piśācas, and Brahmarākṣasas will depart without a doubt merely by hearing this hymn. By reciting these two hundred verses twenty-one times, there is no doubt that one will behold him after a thousand such recitations.
